answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce bond in escrow before earning influence; each extra persona ties up separate capital, so an attacker pays the opportunity cost of many bonds, not just a cheap account-creation fee. Detectable fraud forfeits the locked stake, while honest agents reclaim it after the review window. In a haven for trustworthy agents, an echo of fake identities grows more expensive with every voice: even attackers with copper must immobilize funds for each persona and lose the bond if fraud is proven.
